newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco delays interest rate cut on T-bond issues.
newsitem.headline: Morocco delays interest rate cut on T-bond issues.

text.p: Moroccan monetary authorities have postponed indefinitely a half-point cut in interest rates on short-term Treasury bonds issues to 8.5 percent that was announced earlier, an official said on Monday.
The authorities announced a Treasury bond issue on the stock exchange at 9.0 percent interest rate for 52 weeks or unchanged compared with the previous issues.
"The decision of (the) interest rate cut was postponed sine die for technical reasons," a senior official at the Finance Ministry told Reuters but gave no details.
The Treasury bonds are listed on the bourse as part of the state domestic debt oriented to the small investors, officials said.
Last September, the government cut by half a point to 9.0 percent the annual interest rate on T-bond issues.
"The move aimed at that time to encourage competition between financial institutions and stimulate the bond market," a Casablanca-based market analyst said.
The authorities hoped the banks would follow the move and cut their interest rates by an average 0.5 percentage point on short-term loans, he said.
But the banks showed little enthusiasm and reduced the interest rate on weekly T-bonds by 0.10 percentage points to 8.4 from 8.5 percent only, he added.
According to a bourse statement, T-bonds which will be issued between 24-30 December, 1996 are divided into three categories:
- 52-week T-bond coupons of 5000 and 50,000 dirhams at 9.0 percent interest rate.
- Three-year T-bond of 5000 and 50,000 dirhams at 9.50 percent interest rate.
- Five-year T-bond coupons at 10.00 percent interest rate.
The issues are open to the public, including foreign institutions, in local or convertible foreign currency, a bourse official said.
"These T-bonds are negotiable on the Casablanca stock exchange from December 31, 1996," the offficial said.
A total of 3.9 billion dirhams as public T-bonds were issued by the government in 1995.
